content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I connected the RX (6th pin), TX (1st pin), and GND (5th pin) wires on the [company_name] PLC side. On the other end, I used a 9-pin female connector and mapped RX (2nd pin), TX (3rd pin), and GND (5th pin). For the +5V (4th pin on the PLC), which pin should I use on the connector side?
I'm not sure. Are you trying to create a DIY cable?
Direct wiring between plugs isn't enough for this purpose. Specific electronics are built into the connector housing on the [product_name] side.
Understood… I'll purchase an official cable for [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: The user tried creating a custom cable for a [company_name] PLC by manually wiring pin connections and asked for advice regarding the +5V line. Community members clarified that direct wiring is insufficient due to integrated electronics within the official [product_name] cable, resulting in the user's decision to buy the recommended cable instead.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hoped to manually assemble a working communication cable for the PLC by connecting the correct pins and was looking for help on how to properly handle the +5V pin connection.
